preset-manager:
Manages preset selection,
saving to K-Board Pro 4, and
saving user presets in the editor.
You can also drag and drop a JSON file
containing your saved presets here to
import them into the editor
preset-destination:
Select a destination on
K-Board Pro 4 to store your preset.
Destination 1 is selected by default
preset-save-to-device:
Save the current preset to K-Board Pro 4's
preset destination (selected above)
preset-user-save:
Save changes to the
current User preset
to the editor
preset-user-save-as:
Save a copy of the
current preset with a
new name to the editor
preset-user-revert:
Reverts the current preset
to its unedited state
preset-user-delete:
Deletes the current
User preset from
the editor
This cannot be undone.
preset-user-save-as-name:
Give your preset a name.
This is the name you will
see in the Preset Select Menu
preset-user-save-as-save:
Saves your preset into the Editor
You can now select your preset
in the Preset Select Menu
preset-import-close:
Close this dialog window
without importing presets
preset-import-input:
Enter in the unique name
that you want this preset
to be imported as
preset-import-cancel:
Cancel preset importing and
close this dialog
preset-import-import:
Import the renamed presets.
Duplicate or blank preset
names will not be imported
device-status-message:
Shows K-Board Pro 4's connection status and
other important messages
editor-open-preferences:
Opens the Editor preferences,
change editor setting,
update firmware,
export user presets,
reset K-Board Pro 4...
preferences-versions:
Displays the current editor and
device firmware versions and
if updates are available
preferences-export-user-presets:
Export all User presets to a
JSON file that can be later used
to restore your saved presets
preferences-device-midi-thru:
Select a MIDI device to
send K-Board Pro 4 data to.
preferences-device-reset:
Reset K-Board Pro 4 to factory settings.
All device presets and user curves
will be reset to factory settings
editor-keyboard-lower-zone:
Shows the keys that belong to
the Lower Zone (blue)
editor-keyboard-upper-zone:
Shows the keys that belong to
the Upper Zone (purple)
editor-keyboard-zone-handle:
Indicates what key the
upper zone starts on.
Drag to change
editor-zones:
When MPE is ON, a Zone uses one
Master Channel and up to fifteen Member Channels.
When MPE is OFF a Zone uses
one channel for all Zone MIDI messages
editor-zone-split-key:
Sets where one zone ends, and the other begins.
By default, only the Lower Zone is enabled.
Range: 1 - 48
editor-zone-channels:
Available when MPE mode is set to ON.
Set the number of channels that
the selected MPE zone will use.
editor-zone-channel:
Available when MPE is set to OFF.
Set the MIDI channel that the
selected zone will send on
editor-zone-curve:
Select the Velocity Curve
for the selected Zone.
Select -- Edit Curves -- to open
up the Velocity Curve Editor
editor-velocity-curves-curves: Load a template curve into the curve editor
editor-velocity-curves-editor-windows:
Draw a new curve.
You must disable Touch Support
on your device to be
able to draw a curve
editor-velocity-curves-user: Select the user curve you wish to edit
editor-velocity-curves-destination-label:
Your curve is stored on the K-Board Pro 4
in one of 4 memory locations
editor-velocity-curves-destinations:
Choose the destination to
save your curve
editor-velocity-curves-user-save:
Save the curve to the selected
destination on K-Board Pro 4
editor-velocity-curves-user-reset:
Reset the current curve to its
last saved state
editor-tab-keys-zones:
Click here to access
settings for Key Axes & Zones,
allowing you to customize what
MIDI messages get sent out
editor-tab-sliders-pedals:
Click here to access
settings for Sliders & Pedals,
allowing you to customize what
MIDI messages get sent out
editor-tab-advanced:
Click here to access
settings for various more
advanced K-Board Pro 4 features
editor-key-x-axis:
Customize what MIDI message
gets sent out when moving
left <--> right on a key
editor-key-y-axis:
Customize what MIDI message
gets sent out when moving
up / down on a key
editor-key-z-axis:
Customize what MIDI message
gets sent out when continually
pressing on a key
editor-key-axis-mode:
Select the MIDI message
type for this Key Axis
editor-key-axis-cc:
Available when Axis Mode is set to CC,
enter the CC to send on
editor-key-axis-gain:
Adds gain (or attenuation) to Axis output.
In Relative mode, gain and attenuation are
applied equally in the positive and
negative directions.
range: 0 - 2.00
editor-key-axis-threshold:
Axis output messages are suppressed
until the distance from zero
(or Start in Relative mode) exceeds
the Threshold value.
range: 0 - 127
editor-key-axis-start:
In Relative mode, Axis output
begins at this value and all
output for the duration of the keypress
centers around it. Gain is
calculated with Start considered to be zero and
values above and below treated as growing
in the positive or negative direction.
range: 0 - 127
editor-key-axis-offset:
This value is added to the
Axis output after Gain is applied.
range: -127 - 127
editor-key-axis-curve:
Select a curve to
apply to the axis data
editor-key-axis-zero-on-release:
With this turned on,
a value of zero will be
sent for the data of the
axis when you release a key
editor-key-axis-invert:
With this turned on,
the output values will be reversed
for this axis
editor-sliders:
Define the behavior of
the 4 horizontal sliders
editor-slider-mode-preset-warning:
For smooth preset switching,
verify that all target presets
have the same slider set to
Preset Select mode
editor-slider-cc:
Set the CC value the
slider will send.
range: 0 - 127
editor-slider-zone:
Select the Zone that the
slider will send on the
Zone’s master channel
editor-pedals-p1:
Pedal 1 is a switch/momentary
pedal input and behaves like a
sustain pedal when CC is set to 64
editor-pedals-p2: Pedal 2 is a Expression/continuous pedal input
editor-pedal-mode:
Select the pedal mode,
Off or CC
editor-pedal-cc:
Set the CC value the
pedal will send.
range: 0 - 127
editor-pedal-threshold:
When the incoming value exceeds
this value, a CC with a value of
127 will be sent.
range: 0 - 127
editor-pedal-zone:
Select the Zone that the
pedal will send on the
Zone’s master channel
editor-advanced-mpe:
Toggle MPE On or Off for
entire K-Board Pro 4.
When MPE is Off, Zones will
send MIDI on the Zone Channel
specified in Keys & Zones.
editor-advanced-octave:
Shifts the base octave up or dow
for keys in the selected Zone.
Range depends on if a Slider is
set to an Octave mode.
Octave 4: range: 3 - 6
Octave 7/No Slider: range: 1 - 7
editor-advanced-transpose:
Adds semitone offset to
keys in the selected Zone.
range: 0 - 12
editor-advanced-key-threshold:
Adjusts the amount of pressure
needed to trigger keys.
Higher values require more pressure,
lower values require less.
range: 0 - 254
editor-advanced-release-velocity:
When ON, note-off messages are
sent with the last pressure value
recorded before the note is released.
When release velocity is OFF,
note-off messages are sent with a velocity of 64
editor-advanced-release-velocity-curve:
Apply a curve to
release velocity data
editor-advanced-slider-sensitivity:
Controls how easy it is
to activate the sliders.
Higher values make it more
difficult to trigger the sliders.
Value defaults to 50
editor-advanced-slider-led-mode:
Set the slider LEDs to
Full or Reduced brightness
editor-advanced-mapping-assistant:
Use this for mapping DAW parameters
to the MIDI messages that the
K-Board Pro 4 will output during play
editor-advanced-mapping-assistant-type:
Select message type that a
Key Axis is set to and that
you want the K-Board Pro 4 to send to
your DAW for parameter mapping
editor-advanced-mapping-assistant-channe:
Set the channel for the message that
the K-Board Pro 4 will send
editor-advanced-mapping-assistant-send:
The K-Board Pro 4 will send out a single
message of the selected type and channel
editor-advanced-pitch-bend-slider-range:
Adjusts Global Pitch Bend Range for this Zone.
Global Pitch Bend can be assigned to any slider
editor-advanced-pitch-bend-key-range:
Adjusts Key Pitch Bend Range for this Zone.
Key Pitch Bend can be assigned to any Key Axis
editor-advanced-pitch-bend-return-mode:
Return Mode causes each Key Pitch Bend to
always slew back to zero. This is especially
helpful when using Key Pitch Bend for vibrato
editor-advanced-pitch-bend-return-time:
Return Time specifies the speed of the
Return Mode slew. Larger values make longer,
slower bends easier to execute.
Lower values can make quick vibrato gestures
sound tighter and more controlled.
range: 0.0 - 1.1
editor-advanced-pitch-bend-return-curve:
Apply a curve to shape the
pitch bend data as it returns to 0
editor-sensor-adjustment-open:
Use Sensor Adjustment to
override key on/off thresholds and
factory sensor calibration
editor-sensor-adjustment-octave:
Choose the K-Board Pro 4 octave
you want to adjust sensors for
editor-sensor-adjustment-legend:
Color legend to indicate what
values the sensor colors represent
editor-sensor-adjustment-sensors:
Click on a sensor and then adjust its values below to override factory calibration.
This can be used to finetune the way K-Board Pro 4 responds to your fingers
editor-sensor-adjustment-edit-mode:
Select an edit mode to make changes
to groups of sensors simultaneously
editor-sensor-adjustment-gain:
Adjust tapered gain to amplify
the sensor response at light presses.
range: 0 - 100
editor-sensor-adjustment-max:
Adjust sensor headroom
lower values will 'max out' the sensor
response at lighter pressures,
higher values will allow
more nuance in the upper-range
of sensor response, but can make it
harder to reach note-on
velocities of 127.
range: 0 - 254
editor-sensor-adjustment-on:
Sensor threshold at which the Key turns on
and note-on message is sent.
range: 0 - 254
editor-sensor-adjustment-damp:
Sensor threshold where Axis
reporting turns on/off.
range: 0 - 254
editor-sensor-adjustment-off:
Threshold at which the Key turns off and
a note-off message is sent.
range: 0 - 254
editor-sensor-adjustment-save:
Save all changes to device.
Modified Gain and Max values will
override the factory calibration and
modified Key Thresholds will override the
All Key Threshold preset parameter
editor-sensor-adjustment-revert:
Reverts edits from this
session to previous values
editor-sensor-adjustment-reset:
Removes all user adjustments.
Gain and Max return to factory calibration
and Key Thresholds respond to the
All Key Threshold preset parameter
